ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Burkitt lymphoma: 2

Molecular testing in a rapidly proliferating B-cell lymphoma identifies dysregulation of a transcription factor that drives cell growth. Which oncogenic pathway is most characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma rather than a general marker of inflammation?

  1. t(8;14) involving MYC and the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus
  2. Tingible-body macrophages among proliferating tumor cells
  3. Tumor lysis syndrome
  4. MYC activation
  5. Burkitt lymphoma
Answer and explanation

MYC activation

Dysregulated MYC promotes the rapid proliferation characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.

Option explanations

MYC activation: Dysregulated MYC promotes the rapid proliferation characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma.

Burkitt lymphoma: A rapidly growing mature B-cell lymphoma with MYC rearrangement and a very high proliferative rate fits Burkitt lymphoma. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

t(8;14) involving MYC and the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus: This is the classic translocation; variant immunoglobulin-locus translocations also occur. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Tingible-body macrophages among proliferating tumor cells: Macrophages containing apoptotic debris create the pale stars in the starry-sky pattern. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Tumor lysis syndrome: Rapid cell breakdown can produce hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperuricemia and kidney injury before or after therapy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
